candidate.answerReason: The kth square layer adds 4(k−1) diamonds. Starting with the central diamond, F20 contains 1 + 4(1 + 2 + ⋯ + 19) = 761 diamonds.

methods.label: Count the diamonds in each new layer
methods.explanation:
Count the diamonds added on each new square, since all the earlier diamonds remain. The figure \(F_1\) has one central diamond. The outside square of \(F_2\) has two diamonds on each side, at its corners. Each later square has one more diamond per side, so the outside square of \(F_k\) has \(k\) diamonds on each side.

For \(k\ge2\), counting all four sides gives \(4k\), but each of the four corner diamonds has been counted twice. Subtracting one extra count per corner gives
\[
4k-4=4(k-1)
\]
new diamonds. Different square layers contain different diamonds, so adding these counts includes every diamond exactly once.

Consequently, \(F_{20}\) contains
\[
1+4(1+2+\cdots+19)
\]
diamonds. To evaluate the sum, pair \(1\) with \(19\), \(2\) with \(18\), and so on. There are nine pairs totaling \(20\) each, with \(10\) left in the middle. Thus
\[
1+2+\cdots+19=9\cdot20+10=190.
\]
The total is \(1+4\cdot190=\boxed{761}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The method derives the layer count directly from the construction and evaluates the arithmetic sum by pairing. No formal sequence formulas are assumed.

Nine pairs totaling 20 and the middle term 10 give 190, hence 761. Multiplicities and completeness are explained.
